endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Non-retaliation assurances are formal, written commitments by the HDO that no adverse action will be taken against anyone who in good faith reports a concern about a health AI system, attempted to report one, participates in an investigation, or refuses to use an AI solution they reasonably believe is unsafe.

endorsements.title: Understanding and Addressing Bias in Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Primer for the Emergency Medicine Physician
endorsements.issuer: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
endorsements.quote: The establishment of clear policies for algorithm auditing, validation, and retraining and mechanisms for reporting suspected bias and providing ongoing clinician training are vital for addressing bias.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether written non-retaliation commitments increase reporting of AI concerns or reduce coerced use of unsafe AI, and no supplied study documents the hazard itself. The recommendation rests on one governance framework and one clinical commentary.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. The two endorsements, a CHAI governance playbook and an emergency medicine commentary, are expert opinion. Under GRADE conventions, expert opinion does not supply a certainty rating for an effect, so the effect of this practice on reporting or harm remains unmeasured.

The recommendation assumes that fear of retaliation suppresses reports of AI errors and that some staff feel pressed to use tools they judge unsafe. No supplied study measures how often either occurs, and none shows that a written commitment changes staff behavior or brings errors to light before they reach patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that first measure how often staff withhold AI safety concerns or use AI they consider unsafe, and then compare reporting volume, report quality, and downstream patient harm between organizations or units with and without written non-retaliation commitments. Such studies should also record whether the commitments are enforced when staff invoke them.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Organizations serving these populations cannot tell from this evidence whether the commitment affects the safety of AI used in their care.
